summary.headline: Praj Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT before exceptionals fell to Rs 15.4 mn from Rs 582.5 mn; Q4 order intake Rs 6,580 mn, backlog Rs 43,050 mn.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 8,445 mn versus Rs 8,598 mn a year earlier, while PAT fell to Rs 116 mn from Rs 398 mn. FY26 revenue was Rs 31,679 mn (vs Rs 32,280 mn) and PAT was Rs 238 mn (vs Rs 289 mn). Management attributed margin pressure mainly to site execution cost escalation on delayed projects, continued investment in Praj GenX, and non-business one-time items, rather than raw material prices. Order intake was weak, with several engineering and GenX inquiries (about Rs 300 mn+ inquiry basket) deferred on raw material price uncertainty.

segments.name: Bioenergy
segments.commentary: 67% of FY26 revenue and 86% of Q4 order intake; 78% of backlog. Greenfield 1G fuel ethanol demand slowed, with smaller brownfield, DCO co-product and ENA greenfield orders partly offsetting.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: 22% of FY26 revenue; 2% of Q4 order intake and 16% of backlog. Several opportunities deferred from Q4 on raw material uncertainty, now expected to reflect in FY27.

segments.name: PHS (ZLD/PHS businesses)
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue; 12% of Q4 order intake and 5% of backlog. One joint order closed with a semiconductor company in the current quarter.

segments.name: Praj GenX
segments.commentary: Fixed overhead run rate about Rs 10 crore per month. Data centre modular cooling order (Rs 50-150 crore range by size) under final negotiation, expected in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects an improved performance in FY27, citing bioenergy technology edge and modularisation capability.
Ordering expected to return to a Rs 800-900 crore band on a steady-state basis (management said this is a ballpark, not guidance).
First bio-IBA order expected in Q1 FY27.
GenX break-even targeted in FY27, contingent on booking orders over the next two to three quarters.
Management believes execution challenges are largely resolved and FY27 focus is operational excellence; 'to a great extent the worst is over'.
Blending mandates expected within about one year per management; E22/E25/E27/E30 BIS fuel specifications now notified.
capex_capacity: Praj GenX facility (Mangalore) is large and sophisticated; utilisation expected to rise with data centre and LNG/oil and gas orders.
Client certifications for the Mangalore facility rose to about 12-13 clients from about nine at end of Q3 FY26.
CBG capacity ramp-up underway at a few plants using Napier grass and rice straw mixed feedstock.
R&D spend in FY26 about Rs 65-66 crore, of which about Rs 20 crore capex (lab and equipment) and about Rs 45-46 crore opex (in other expenses).
Basic engineering order for one ethanol-to-SAF plant for an international customer being completed; detailed engineering order under discussion.
demand_pricing: Q4 raw material costs rose about 3% on a consolidated basis, offset partly by a 2% fall in other expenses; net margin impact about 1-1.5%. Management said the larger pressure was site-related execution cost escalation.
YTD raw material prices broadly flat per management; contracting has moved from 100% fixed-price to some flexibility on raw material price changes.
About Rs 300 mn+ of inquiries deferred from Q4 due to raw material price and supply chain uncertainty.
Government roadmap: 150 E85/E100 outlets in Delhi, Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur within a month, 500 within 6-12 months, and 5,000 E100 stations within 24 months.
Export revenues were 36% of FY26 revenue. Positive biofuel policy signals in the US (15% ethanol blend bill passed by House), Indonesia, Vietnam, Kenya, Latin America and others.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins and profits declined over three years despite R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBP-20 capacity build-out ended, reducing greenfield ethanol plant orders, while GenX investment over 2.5-3 years held back profits; order books are expected to benefit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did raw material inflation hit Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said raw material costs rose about 3% in Q4 with other expenses down 2%, net impact 1-1.5%; the main driver was site execution cost escalation linked to project delays. YTD raw material costs were broadly flat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the deferred order quantum and GenX outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred inquiries were about Rs 300 mn+ (called an inquiry basket, not orders). GenX data centre order ranges Rs 50-150 crore; GenX fixed overhead run rate about Rs 10 crore per month; break-even targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for mandates beyond E20 and what is the ethanol capacity impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mandates likely within one year. Blends of 2-5% could be met by existing capacity with efficiency gains; above 5% needs new capacity, which Praj is ready to supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected steady-state order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports a Rs 800-900 crore range typically, but stopped short of formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the R&D spend and the synergy between bioenergy and data centres?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 R&D about Rs 65-66 crore (about Rs 20 crore capex, Rs 45-46 crore opex, about 100 scientists). Data centre work is cooling skids and modules; long term, bioenergy could power medium and large data centres.

risks_watch: Execution cost escalation and open sites; management says challenges are resolved but Q4 PBT was only Rs 15.4 mn.
Raw material and supply chain volatility on fixed-price contracts, with deferred inquiries pending price visibility.
Timing of blending mandate notifications (E22-E30) and E85/E100 outlet rollout; management said delays remain possible.
Conversion of GenX data centre order expected in Q1 FY27 and bio-IBA first order in Q1 FY27.
Greenfield 1G ethanol slowdown and funding delays extending project execution cycles.
Leadership restructuring with the MD and JMD/CFO roles; a shareholder asked about buyback and bonus options (Board matter).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the policy and technology outlook, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins and order inflow; several answers were qualitative and avoided numbers. Management repeatedly pointed to upcoming FY27 milestones without firm timelines.
key_quotes: Overall impact is 1 -1.5% additional which we have incurred.
So, to a great extent the worst is over.
We believe that it will be not longer than one year, but really to predict it in terms of exact months is difficult for us.
Earlier, our all contracts used to be 100% fixed price.

growth.why: Management expects improved FY27 performance, but gives no numeric revenue guidance; backing is partial (Rs 43,050 mn backlog, first bio-IBA order and data-centre order expected Q1 FY27, but Rs 800-900 cr order band explicitly 'not guidance' and Rs 300 mn+ inquiries deferred), and Q4 revenue fell about 2% with PBT before exceptionals down sharply.
